threat_assessment:
You are ignored until one of three things shows. Count them, because a human table's reading flips on each and the Forge AI's does not.

1. Smothering Tithe over an empty board. In log 002 (v1.2.1) the Tithe and Kami of the Crescent Moon were netting about three Treasure a cycle and you were the target at once, with no creatures out. Stated assumption: a human table reads Treasure as a clock. The Forge AI does not: over 300 pooled games it attacked the seat that had dealt the most combat damage in 0.6625 of decisions and the lowest-life seat in 0.5447, and this deck dealt a median 0.5 combat damage, so in Forge you are attacked as the low life total. What to do: land a taxer first (Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes; assembled 0.496, 0.357 by turn six) or a flier blocker (Drift of Phantasms, Archangel, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Kefnet; 0.68, 0.529 by turn six), or hold the Tithe until one is down. The Second Doctor's end-step draw stops each opponent who takes it from attacking you next turn.

2. The first Approach resolving. You gain 7 life in public and every seat knows the second cast wins. Assume every held answer appears when you present it, and count open mana before you cast. Weight inaction heaviest: an opponent who passed with two open and let your engine resolve is unlikely to hold the counter. Hold Swan Song or Dovin's Veto for the Approach turn and not before (stack 002; Dovin's Veto cannot be countered). Fierce Guardianship is free only while you control a commander.

3. The flip. Heliod, the Warped Eclipse on the battlefield reads flash and discount to anyone who picks up the card. The back face appeared in 35 of 120 games; Heliod resolved in 68. Losing him took the engine offline in log 001 (a countered counter, then Swords redirected onto him) and in log 002 (your own Supreme Verdict). Insurance: Lightning Greaves, Karametra's Blessing, Guardian of Faith, Teferi's Protection, Leyline of Anticipation (assembled 0.683, 0.531 by turn six). Forge cast Guardian and Teferi's Protection zero times, so its read on the package is a floor. Whether Greaves' shroud blocks your own Blessing, and which pieces survive your own wipe, each needs a stack scenario. Wipe first, then resolve Heliod.

Against a combo seat the rule inverts: held answers rot, and the last profitable moment is now (log 002, Cranko). Horn of Greed draws that seat a card per land drop. Count its cards before you deploy a gift piece.
matchups:
Every Forge figure here is the v1.2.1 run: 120 games, standard pod (giada-angels, baylen-tokens, abaddon), 2026-09-09, three cards behind the sleeved list. Nothing measures Isochron Scepter, Horn of Greed or Mind Stone.

Go-wide fliers (giada-angels). The matchup that ends you: 43 of your 61 damage eliminations; combat damage taken mean 37.92 against 3.28 dealt. You cannot race three life totals, so you tax and block. Deploy: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes. Hold: Day of Judgment and Supreme Verdict until their board is the reason, and never with Heliod on the battlefield. 30 of giada's 32 creatures fly, so Kefnet blocks only with seven cards in hand. The card that flips it: Archangel of Tithes, a taxer and a flying blocker in one slot.

Counter-heavy control (log 001, Alex). The danger is the stack war on the Approach turn, not your board. Hold: one counter for the win turn, and cast nothing into open blue you have not counted. Deploy: Dovin's Veto (cannot be countered) and Force of Negation (free on their turn for a blue card). New at v1.3.0: Isochron Scepter imprinting Swan Song or Dovin's Veto is a counter every turn for {2}; unmeasured, and the activation is not discounted. The card that flips it: Dovin's Veto.

Combo (log 002, Cranko). Held answers rot here; counter the setup, not the finisher. Eight counterspells, two of them free. Deploy: Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora, which bill casts (410 and 511 trigger lines). Hold: the gift. Forced Fruition was cut for handing a combo seat seven cards a spell; Horn of Greed still draws them one per land. The card that flips it: Fierce Guardianship, free while Heliod is on the battlefield.

Stax and taxes. This attacks your edge directly: 22 two-drops and 18 three-drops cast at a discount, so a Sphere effect is the discount reversed and a no-flash piece blanks the back face. Outs: Disenchant, Cathar Commando, Loran of the Third Path, Cyclonic Rift, Otawara. Graveyard and land pieces are uncovered (deck-audit, 3 of 5 classes). Under a lock you are the beatdown with a seven-mana sorcery for a clock: tutor Approach early with Long-Term Plans (log 002).

Grinding value (abaddon, baylen-tokens). 11 and 7 eliminations. You are the seat accruing: Consecrated Sphinx draws two per opponent draw (326 trigger lines), Smothering Tithe 998. The card that flips it: Consecrated Sphinx with Howling Mine or Font of Mythos out. Whether Alhammarret's Archive makes that four cards needs a stack scenario.
how_it_wins:
You win by casting Approach of the Second Sun twice from your hand. The first cast gains 7 life and puts the card seventh from the top; the second wins as it resolves, and stack 002 proves the only place anyone can stop it is on the stack.

Three things have to be true. First, the table is drawing. Eleven permanents hand every player cards: Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran of the Third Path, The Second Doctor, Scrawling Crawler, Horn of Greed. The goldfish draws one in 0.921 of games, mean turn 2.499. Second, the gift is billed back. Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Smothering Tithe, Consecrated Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind turn opponents' draws and casts into your cards and Treasure (2,322 trigger lines in the v1.2.1 Forge run). Heliod, the Warped Eclipse turns their draws into a discount, {1} off each spell per card they drew this turn, and lets you cast at instant speed. The discount counts draws THIS turn, so it lives on their turns, where a flash deck casts; a generic-cost artifact such as Mind Stone or Isochron Scepter reads as free behind two opponent draws. That is oracle text, not a resolved board: needs a stack scenario. Third, you pay {6}{W} twice. Goldfish mean available mana crosses seven between turn 7 (6.412) and turn 8 (7.064), discount unmodelled.

The v1.2.1 run (120 games) says where the difficulty sits: 27 games saw a first Approach, 12 a second, and all 12 second casts won. 20 wins of 99 decided, 0.202, ci95 [0.135, 0.292]; 8 of the 20 were the table losing without Approach. No game, Forge or paper, has been played on v1.3.0.

The misread: the table files you as the group-hug seat. Heliod is the converter, not the threat. The back face appeared in 35 of 120 games and 10 of the 12 Approach wins came without it. Do not rush him out. Wipe first, then resolve him (log 002).

combo_lines.002:
This line turns on one word: cast. Approach's win clause asks whether you have CAST another spell with that name this game. It tracks an event in the game's history, not the card, so the first Approach going seventh from the top and becoming a new object (CR 400.7) does not undo it.

The check is an instruction you follow during resolution (CR 608.2c), not a state-based action, and no player has priority while a spell is resolving (CR 117.2e). So the window is exactly the stack. A counter there sends Approach to the graveyard with no life gain and no win check (CR 701.6a). Swan Song answers that counter; it does not answer an activated or triggered ability (CR 113.9).

What it proves: the second cast wins through one counterspell if you hold Swan Song, at sorcery speed, for the full {6}{W}.

What it does not prove: Mystical Tutor is premise, not a resolved step. The end-step cast under Heliod's flash, and the discounted price (log 002: "two or three, not seven"), each need a stack scenario. Ancient Tomb on the board is no longer in the deck; the ruling does not rest on it.

card_roles.Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the: Front face is a 4/4 that rebuys an enchantment from your graveyard; the back face is the reason you play him, granting flash to everything and cutting {1} off your spells for each card your opponents drew this turn. Transform when you can spend {3}{U/P} without giving up the turn — every Howling Mine trigger is three opposing draws and three mana off your bill.
card_roles.Aetherflux Reservoir: The ceiling. It gains you life per spell per turn and turns 50 of that life into 50 damage at any target, and stack 006 proves the full three-opponent kill off it. Deploy it as a life cushion in the normal game and take the kill only when the loop pieces arrive with it.
card_roles.Alhammarret's Archive: Doubles your draws and your life gain and nobody else's, which is the exact asymmetry this deck is short of. Play it into a board that already has a donation engine down, not before.
card_roles.An Offer You Can't Refuse: One mana to counter a noncreature spell, and the two Treasures you hand back cost you almost nothing in a game you intend to win on upkeep triggers. Use it on the commit turn, not on the first ramp spell you see.
card_roles.Approach of the Second Sun: Your most reliable ending. Cast it once for the 7 life and the seventh-from-the-top setup, then defend the second cast — stack 002 shows the only window opponents get is while it sits on the stack.
card_roles.Arcane Denial: Counter anything and let them draw two; you replace your own card at the next upkeep. Fire it freely, because two extra cards in an opponent's hand is exactly what Iron Maiden bills for.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Two-mana fixing that produces either colour, and one of the two cheap rocks the verified loop runs on (stacks 004, 006). Cast it on turn two and remember it is a combo piece later.
card_roles.Azorius Signet: The second colour-fixing rock, and it filters generic mana into exactly the {W}{U} the double-pip spells want. Play it early; it is what makes a turn-four Teferi cast on turn four.
card_roles.Braingeyser: Point X cards at yourself for the fuel or at an opponent to shove their hand past Ebony Owl Netsuke's seven-card line before their upkeep. Save it for the turn a punisher is already down.
card_roles.Consecrated Sphinx: Two cards every time any opponent draws one, in a deck that makes all three opponents draw extra every turn. It will eat removal — hold interaction the turn you cast it, or cast it with the counter already up.
card_roles.Counterspell: Two blue, counter anything, no conditions. Spend it on the spell that ends the game or ends your engine, never on the flashy one.
card_roles.Cyclonic Rift: The reset. Overload it at the end of the turn before yours and take the board away from three players at once — this is also your answer to a stax board you cannot otherwise unstick.
card_roles.Dictate of Kruphix: Every player draws an extra card each draw step, and flash lets you land it at end of turn with counter mana still up. It is a donation engine — pair it with a punisher or you are just being generous.
card_roles.Dig Through Time: Delve makes it cheap in a deck that fills its own graveyard, and two cards from the top seven is how you find a punisher or the Approach. Cast it on a turn you were holding mana anyway.
card_roles.Displacer Kitten: Blinks one of your permanents on every noncreature cast — Sol Ring comes back untapped, Loran re-triggers, Mystic Remora returns fresh. Its infinite-mana reputation is refuted by stack 005, so play it for the value it obviously does.
card_roles.Dovin's Veto: Counters a noncreature spell and cannot be countered itself, which makes it your best answer to another blue deck's protection. Hold it for their commit turn.
card_roles.Drannith Magistrate: Shuts off every opponent cast that is not from hand — command zone, graveyard, exile, all of it. Deploy it against commander-reliant tables and expect to defend it.
card_roles.Ebony Owl Netsuke: Four damage to each opponent holding seven or more cards, on their own upkeep. Stack 003 confirms it checks seven both when it triggers and when it resolves — so fill their hand before their turn, not during it.
card_roles.Faerie Mastermind: Flash, flying, and a card every time an opponent draws their second in a turn, which in this deck is most turns. Its {3}{U} table-draw mode is a punisher enabler you can use at instant speed.
card_roles.Fierce Guardianship: Free counterspell while you control your commander — the single best card in your hand on the turn you tapped out. Cast Heliod before you tap low, so this stays live.
card_roles.Folio of Fancies: Deletes maximum hand size for everyone, which uncaps what Iron Maiden and Viseling charge, and its {X}{X} mode fills every hand at once. The mill mode is a real backup kill against one player.
card_roles.Font of Mythos: Two extra cards per player per draw step — the heaviest donation effect in the deck. Do not cast it without a punisher on the battlefield or already in hand.
card_roles.Force of Negation: Free on an opponent's turn if you pitch a blue card, which is how you protect an engine on the turn you had no mana. Keep a spare blue card in hand rather than emptying it.
card_roles.Forced Fruition: Every opponent spell hands its caster seven cards. That is enormous punisher fuel and it is also a real gift — stack 003 verifies the seven arrive even if they kill the enchantment in response, so land it when the punishers can convert it.
card_roles.Grand Abolisher: During your turn opponents cannot cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures or enchantments. That is the shield for your commit turn — deploy him the turn before, or lead with him.
card_roles.Howling Mine: Two mana, one extra card for everyone each draw step, and the cheapest way to start the donation half. It is a turn-two play only if you have the punisher to follow it.
card_roles.Hullbreaker Horror: Flash, uncounterable, and a bounce trigger on every spell you cast — and the one irreplaceable card in the verified kill. As a fair card it is a seven-mana wall that bounces a problem permanent every turn, which is most of what you will actually get from it.
card_roles.Iron Maiden: Hand size minus 4 to each opponent, on each opponent's upkeep, computed on resolution. Three mana for a clock that bills three players — this is the card the whole donation half exists to feed.
card_roles.Jace Beleren: The +2 draws for everyone, which feeds the punishers and Heliod's discount at once; the −1 draws you a card while the loyalty holds. Tick him up unless you specifically need the card now.
card_roles.Jace, Wielder of Mysteries: Draws while threatening to convert an empty library into a win, and he survives your own Supreme Verdict. Treat the empty-library win as an emergency exit, not a plan — nothing in the record walks it.
card_roles.Kami of the Crescent Moon: Two mana for an extra card per player per draw step. Cheapest donation engine on the curve, and a body the table has to decide whether to bother killing.
card_roles.Kwain, Itinerant Meddler: Taps to let each player draw and gain 1, which reads as a favour and is an upkeep bill. Use it every turn once a punisher is down, and skip it entirely when one is not.
card_roles.Leyline of Anticipation: Free on turn zero from your opening hand, and it makes everything you cast flash — which means every turn you spend holding counter mana can also deploy a threat.
card_roles.Long-Term Plans: The only unrestricted search in the deck, and the only card that can find Hullbreaker Horror. It puts the card third from the top, so cast it a turn or two before you need the piece.
card_roles.Loran of the Third Path: Destroys an artifact or enchantment on entry, taps to draw you and one opponent a card, and re-triggers on every Displacer Kitten blink. She is your most repeatable answer to a stax piece.
card_roles.Mathemagics: Draws 2^X, which is the biggest single hand-fill in the deck. Point it at an opponent with the punishers down and you are choosing exactly how much their upkeep costs.
card_roles.Metallurgic Summonings: An X/X Construct on every instant or sorcery you cast, which turns your draw-go turns into a board. It is how a permission deck stops being defenceless.
card_roles.Mystic Remora: One mana, and it draws off opposing noncreature spells unless they pay {4}. Play it early and let the cumulative upkeep kill it once it has drawn three or four — that is a fine trade.
card_roles.Mystical Tutor: Puts an instant or sorcery on top, which in practice means it fetches Approach of the Second Sun for the winning cast. Use it at end of turn so your draw step collects it.
card_roles.Path to Exile: One mana, exiles any creature, and the basic land they get is a price worth paying to answer a commander now. Keep it for the creature that actually kills you.
card_roles.Pearl Medallion: Cuts {1} off your white spells, which stacks with Heliod's per-draw discount on the turns the table is drawing. It discounts nothing colourless — the loop rocks are unaffected (stack 004).
card_roles.Propaganda: Every attacker costs {2} to send at you, and it blanks attack plans from three players for one card. Cast it before you need it, not after the board is wide.
card_roles.Prosperity: X cards for each player. Fill three hands in one shot, then let Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke charge all three at their own upkeeps.
card_roles.Psychosis Crawler: Drains each opponent 1 per card you draw, and its size is your hand size. In a deck with draw doublers this is genuine reach — it just needs to survive a turn cycle.
card_roles.Rhystic Study: The tax everyone knows and nobody pays. Ask every time; the card is worth more than the awkwardness, and the {1} they pay is tempo you take anyway.
card_roles.Sapphire Medallion: Cuts {1} off your blue spells, and this deck is 61 blue pips across 40 cards, so it discounts almost everything you cast. It does not discount the colourless loop rocks (stack 004).
card_roles.Scrawling Crawler: Draws every player a card on your upkeep and drains each opponent 1 whenever they draw. It is a donation engine and a punisher in the same card, which is unusual enough to prioritise.
card_roles.Skyscribing: X cards for every player, plus a forecast mode that hands out one card a turn from your hand for {2}{U}. The forecast is the sleeper — it keeps hands topped up without you spending a card.
card_roles.Smothering Tithe: A Treasure every time an opponent draws and declines to pay {2}, in a deck that makes them draw constantly. Treat it as ramp: it is one of your 39 mana sources.
card_roles.Sol Ring: One mana, taps for two, and it is one of the cheap rocks the verified loop runs on. Cast it turn one every single time.
card_roles.Sphinx's Tutelage: Mills two per card you draw and repeats on a colour match, which in a deck this draw-dense is a real alternate clock on one opponent. Aim it at whoever you least want drawing.
card_roles.Stroke of Genius: Instant-speed X cards at any player. End of turn, point it at the opponent whose upkeep is next and they walk into the punishers holding a fresh hand.
card_roles.Supreme Verdict: Uncounterable board wipe, and your four planeswalkers survive it. Cast it when the table has overextended into your pillow effects, not the first time you are attacked.
card_roles.Swan Song: One mana to counter an enchantment, instant or sorcery; they get a 2/2 flier. It is your counter-to-the-counter on the turn you cast Approach of the Second Sun (stack 002).
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: The cheapest creature answer in the game and the life they gain rarely matters against a deck that wins on upkeep triggers. Save it for a commander.
card_roles.Talisman of Progress: Two-mana rock that pays either colour for a point of life. It exists to make your turn-three double-pip spells cast on turn three.
card_roles.Teferi's Ageless Insight: Doubles every draw after the first in your draw step, which stacks with Alhammarret's Archive. It also doubles the triggers on Psychosis Crawler and Sphinx's Tutelage.
card_roles.Teferi's Protection: Your life total cannot change, you gain protection from everything, and your board phases out. Hold it for the turn a wipe or a lethal swing would otherwise end you — it is a whole turn of immunity.
card_roles.Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim: Gains loyalty on every card you draw, so he grows himself in this deck, and his −2 makes a Spirit that grows on every draw too. He lives through Supreme Verdict; deploy him into a board you intend to wipe.
card_roles.Temple Bell: Taps to draw the whole table a card. Cheap, colourless, and repeatable — ring it every turn once a punisher is down, and leave it untapped when one is not.
card_roles.The Second Doctor: Deletes maximum hand size for everyone and offers each player a card at your end step; anyone who accepts cannot attack you next turn. Every answer they give you profits you, which is the whole point of the card.
card_roles.Thought Vessel: Two-mana rock that also removes your own maximum hand size, so the X-draw spells you point at yourself are not wasted. It taps for colourless — it does not move your colour counts.
card_roles.Torrential Gearhulk: Flashes in and recasts an instant from your graveyard for free, which on a draw-go turn is a counterspell plus a 5/6. Cast it on an opponent's end step whenever you did not need your mana.
card_roles.Viseling: The same hand-size-minus-4 upkeep bill as Iron Maiden, on a body. It costs more, so it is the second punisher you deploy, not the first.
card_roles.Teferi, Hero of Dominaria: The +1 draws and untaps two lands at the next end step, so your clock advances without ever tapping out; the −3 tucks a problem permanent. In a slow game he is the best card in the deck.
card_roles.Archmage's Charm: Counter, draw two, or steal a one-mana permanent — never a dead card. It also wants {U}{U}{U}, the only triple pip in the deck, so cast it off duals rather than promising it on turn three.
card_roles.Enlightened Tutor: One white mana at instant speed for any artifact or enchantment, which here is Aetherflux Reservoir, a rock, a punisher, Rhystic Study or Smothering Tithe. It puts the card on top, so fetch a turn before you need it.
card_roles.Island: Fourteen copies, and the reason blue is castable at all. It is the land you fetch with Flooded Strand unless a double-white spell is the play.
card_roles.Plains: Three copies against 16 white pips. Keep one in play before you commit to a hand that needs double white.
card_roles.Adarkar Wastes: Untapped either colour for a point of life, or colourless for free. Take the damage on the turns that matter and the free mana on the ones that do not.
card_roles.Ancient Tomb: Two colourless for two life, which is how a four-mana commander lands on turn three. The life is real against aggro — it is not free.
card_roles.Command Tower: Untapped, either colour, no cost. The single best land in the deck.
card_roles.Deserted Beach: Untapped once you control two other lands, so it is a tapland on turns one and two and a dual afterwards. Play it early or not at all.
card_roles.Eiganjo, Seat of the Empire: A white source that can be discarded to shoot an attacking or blocking creature for 4, cheaper for each legendary creature you control. Free insurance in a land slot.
card_roles.Flooded Strand: Fetches a Plains or an Island for a life, which fixes your colour on the exact turn you know which one you need. Crack it in response to something, not on your own main phase.
card_roles.Glacial Fortress: Untapped if you already control a Plains or an Island, which after turn one is nearly always. Effectively a dual.
card_roles.Hallowed Fountain: Pay 2 life and it comes down untapped. Pay it — the tempo is worth more than the life in a deck holding counter mana.
card_roles.Irrigated Farmland: One of two lands that always enters tapped, and it cycles for {2} when you are flooded. Play it on a turn you were not going to spend all your mana.
card_roles.Mana Confluence: Any colour for a life, every turn. It is your cleanest answer to a hand that needs {U}{U}{U} or {W}{W} on the same turn.
card_roles.Mikokoro, Center of the Sea: A colourless land that draws the whole table a card for {2}. It is a donation engine hiding in the mana base — and a blank one until a punisher is down.
card_roles.Otawara, Soaring City: A blue source that channels from hand to bounce an artifact, creature, enchantment or planeswalker, cheaper for each legendary creature you control. Answers a problem permanent without spending a card slot.
card_roles.Prairie Stream: Untapped once you control two or more basic lands, which with 17 basics is usually true by turn three. Before that it is a tapland.
card_roles.Seachrome Coast: Untapped while you control two or fewer other lands — the mirror image of the rest of your conditional duals. Lead with it.
card_roles.Skycloud Expanse: Costs {1} to tap for {W}{U}, so it is a filter rather than a dual. Good on the turns you have spare mana, awkward on the turns you do not.
card_roles.Temple of Enlightenment: The other land that always enters tapped, and it scries 1 on the way in. Drop it on turn one or on a turn you are holding up nothing.

mulligan:
Keep two to five lands. The goldfish keeps 0.737 of first sevens, averages 0.328 mulligans, and 0.981 of kept hands can act by turn three. 4,225 of 10,000 kept hands hold two lands and 3,444 hold three; the turn-three land drop hits 0.868, turn four 0.728, turn six 0.534. Two lands plus one of the seven rocks is a keep. Two lands and no rock is a ship.

Then classify. The enabler is a gift piece, any of the eleven that make the table draw. One in the opener is what a keep is for; a hand without one is drawing to it, and one arrives by turn six in 0.822 of games. The answer is one of eight counterspells: Counterspell, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto, Arcane Denial, Archmage's Charm, Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship. 0.822 of kept hands hold a card from the 21-card interaction suite on turn one. A land pair, one gift piece and one counter is the keep. A land pair, two rocks and no spell is a ship.

Do not keep for the commander. Heliod lands on mean turn 4.187, by turn six in 0.896 of games, and the flip is a second payment ({3}{U/P}) the goldfish reaches by turn six in 0.561. The win is not in the opener either: Approach, Mystical Tutor or Long-Term Plans is drawn by turn six in 0.358 of games, 0.508 with tutors, and the second cast needs seven mana whatever you hold.

Colour: 31 cards want blue against 20 white, and Archmage's Charm wants {U}{U}{U}. Look hardest at a hand whose lands are all Plains.

Ship on sight: three X-spells and no draw engine; Psychosis Crawler with no gift piece (the two Crawlers drained a median 0.0 life a game in the v1.2.1 run); Kefnet the Mindful as your only blocker, since he cannot block under seven cards in hand.
upgrades:
Ten cards, and six of them move a number the audit already flags. The punisher half is six cards, which is 36% of an opening seven. Black Vise makes it seven, and the corpus prices that step at 41%. One card, five points of consistency, one mana — that is the best exchange rate on the list.

Three cards chase a much smaller number for a much bigger prize. The verified kill assembles in 0.7% of games because its creature component holds exactly one card, and a named card is 7.1% of an opening seven. Tidespout Tyrant makes that component two. Teferi, Time Raveler offers Aetherflux Reservoir an engine that does not run through a seven-mana body at all, and Mana Vault is the rock whose ledger might differ from the pair stack 004 settled at exactly neutral. Lightning Greaves is the cheap version of the same worry — it does not raise the assembly rate, it just keeps the one creature alive.

Then the flat spots. Graveyard is one of five permanent classes and the only one no card in the 99 answers; Soul-Guide Lantern closes it for one mana without turning off your own Torrential Gearhulk. Blue sits at 31 sources against a 36 yardstick and white at 20 against 22, and Tundra is the rare card that moves both counts without adding to the tapland column. March of Otherworldly Light covers the three permanent classes your removal only answers on the way in.

The last two are about who your card advantage actually serves. Twenty-two copies of draw is double the floor, but a lot of it feeds four seats at once. Esper Sentinel only ever draws for you, and Windfall converts three no-maximum-hand-size effects into three refilled hands on a turn you pick — which is the difference between hoping the punishers hit big and scheduling it.

Four of the ten carry unsettled questions rather than settled ones. Mana Vault's arithmetic, Tidespout Tyrant's mandatory target, and the Teferi loop all want a stack scenario before anyone treats them as arithmetic.
mana_base:
Thirty-three lands across eighteen entries, and only two of them always enter tapped. Seven can enter tapped at all, and five of those are conditional — a shock you can pay through, or a dual that untaps itself once you control two other lands. Against a template that asks for 37-39, thirty-three is under, and the audit says so.

The land count is not the whole supply. Six rocks take it to 39 mana sources against a 37 target, so the deck is short on lands and at target on mana — and that is before a ritual and three cost-reducers that shrink the bills rather than pay them. In the goldfish, the turn-three land drop hits 86.6% of the time and the turn-six one only 47.1%, while mean available mana still climbs from 3.311 on turn three to 5.325 on turn six. The rocks do the second half of that job.

Blue is 79.2% of the pips and 63.4% of the sources; white is 20.8% of the pips and 36.6% of the sources. That is 61 blue pips spread over 40 cards against 16 white pips over 14 — the deck is far bluer than its mana base is, and white is comfortably over-served. Blue lands at 26, lifting to 31 with rocks, against a 36 yardstick; white at 15, lifting to 20, against 22.

On-curve, that reads as 74.2% blue and 78.7% white off lands alone, and 83.9% and 88.1% once the rocks are counted. The 90% figure is a yardstick, not a possibility at thirty-three lands. The card that feels the five-source blue gap is Archmage's Charm, the only triple pip in the list, which is why it plays like a later card than its mana value suggests.

One quiet detail in the source list: Sol Ring and Thought Vessel produce colourless, so they add to the 39 sources and nothing to either colour count. Smothering Tithe does count for both, which makes the deck's best tax card also a piece of its mana base — a Treasure every time an opponent declines to pay {2}, in a deck built to make opponents draw.
editors_letter:
The deck in this issue hands every player at the table free cards, and then bills them for holding the cards.

That is the whole idea, and it is worth an issue because of how strange the seat feels. You spend your turn making three other people richer, and some of them thank you and mean it. Then, on each of their upkeeps — the step nobody looks at — a piece of cardboard asks how many cards they are holding and takes the difference out of their life total. You will not attack anybody. Your damage arrives while you are doing nothing, which is the only time it can arrive, because your mana is spoken for by the counterspell in your hand.

There is also a spectacular one-turn kill in here, and its reputation is the wrong way round. The Counselor has walked that line end to end and it is real. Ledger has the rate at which it turns up, and it is small enough to change what you do on turn four.

You will have a good time here if your favourite thing in this game is being liked and being unbeatable in the same evening, and if you can enjoy a turn where you do nothing on purpose. You will not, if you want your damage to be your own idea.

Coach Brightside opens by telling you the best card in the plan deals no damage. He gets narrowed for it twice, and the second one is the best thing in the department.

pilots_log.text: Cleanup is stealing from you, not from him. He trims to seven and the damage he owed you goes to the graveyard with the cards. The best card in your punisher plan deals zero damage — and it is not Iron Maiden, and it is certainly not Forced Fruition, the one that hands somebody seven cards at once. It is The Second Doctor, or it is Folio of Fancies. Both read "Players have no maximum hand size," and neither has ever burned anybody for a point in its life. Without one of those two on the battlefield, the eighth card you gift a player gets shaved off before you can charge him for it. You can hand a man seventy cards. Iron Maiden still asks him for three.

On the record, and then narrower than the Coach put it. Twice narrower, and the second one is in his favour.

Stack 003 is that exact board: Forced Fruition, Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke down, no hand-size effect anywhere. An opponent holding two cards casts Naturalize at the Fruition. The trigger goes on the stack above the spell that caused it (603.3) and resolves first (608.1), so they draw seven with the Fruition already doomed — hand one, then eight — and at their own cleanup they discard to seven (514.1, 402.2). The Coach's shave is on the record.

First narrowing: the trim does not blank the rank, it pins it. Ebony Owl Netsuke asks for seven OR MORE, so a hand cut to exactly seven is a hand that satisfies it — a flat 4. Iron Maiden is hand size minus four, which at seven is 3. Stack 003's number for that upkeep is 7 damage, 18 down to 11. It also charged the other opponent 1 on the way past: Iron Maiden triggers on each opponent's upkeep, not only the one you are cross with.

Second narrowing, and read 514.1 again — it is the ACTIVE player who discards. A player trims at their own cleanup step and nowhere else. The shave catches what you gave them in their own draw step, and touches nothing you hand them during the other three turns of the round.

Say that last part again, because it changes what you do with your hands.

Stop tapping Temple Bell on your own turn for value. Stop pointing Mikokoro at the table whenever it is convenient for you. A gift given in a player's own draw step is a gift he throws away at the end of that turn. A gift given at the top of his upkeep is one you are billing him for immediately.

So keep the Bell untapped and hold two mana for Mikokoro. The punisher trigger goes on the stack at his upkeep — that is your window. Everybody draws, his hand gets one fatter, and Iron Maiden counts it. And when you hold both halves, land the thing that charges before you open the tap. A Font of Mythos on an empty board is you buying three strangers a round.

Two of those three, Coach. The middle one has a hole in it that I enjoy.

Iron Maiden and Viseling compute X on resolution — stack 003 is explicit, the number is read off the hand when the ability resolves and not when it triggered. So yes: respond to the trigger, everybody draws, X lands one higher.

Ebony Owl Netsuke is a different animal and Mikokoro cannot reach it. Its seven-or-more clause is an intervening "if": the game checks it when the trigger event occurs, and the ability triggers only if it is true (603.4). A player sitting on six at the beginning of his upkeep has no Netsuke trigger at all — nothing on the stack, nothing to respond to, and no card you hand him afterwards brings it back. Stack 003 walks that exact case at the second opponent's upkeep and the Netsuke never fires.

Plainly: your trick moves the Maiden and the Viseling. The Netsuke has to be right before you get priority.

Ten thousand seeded games, and what the Coach is describing is priced in two halves and never as one machine.

The donation half is ten cards: 53.7% of opening sevens, 63.3% by turn three, drawn in 85.2% of games and 75.4% by turn six, mean turn 2.507. Read that as drawn, not deployed — the simulation counts a card the moment it reaches your hand.

The punisher half is six cards: 36.4% of openers, 67.2% of games, 55.9% by turn six, mean turn 3.045. Both halves together: 56.7%, 41.2% by turn six, mean turn 4.215. The pair is a subset of the donation half, so a band of games reaches turn six giving cards away with nothing charging for them.

Now the part that touches the Coach's opening. The Second Doctor and Folio of Fancies are two of the ten in that donation group, priced as interchangeable with the other eight. No figure measures a game in which one of those two specific cards is present. The file proposes adding them as a third required group. Until somebody runs it, 56.7% describes a machine, and the version the Coach is telling you to build has no rate.

Then here is how you play a number that does not exist yet.

Mulligan toward classes, not cards. Something that gives, something that charges — that is the keep. Two Iron Maidens and no engine is a blank seven, and you find out on turn four, when three people are drawing normally and you are holding a museum piece.

And once you are past the threshold, stop accumulating. The turn a punisher joins an engine you are charging rent, and every turn you hold something back to be safe is a free draw step you are handing the table.

While the Coach gives orders off stack 003, I should tell the reader what the file says about stack 003.

It passed. Every step is cited and supported, and it walks the deck's median plan to an exact life total. And the arrow it ought to support — the donation stage feeding the punisher stage — is drawn dashed, which here means unproven, which means none of us may state it as fact.

The reason is not doubt. The join that decides whether a stack backs an arrow reads the stack, the hand and the graveyard, and stops once two card names clear the bar. On 003 the two names it finds are Naturalize and Arcane Denial. Naturalize is the opponent's card and is not in this 99, and the board — where Forced Fruition, Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke are actually standing — is never consulted. Nine of this deck's thirteen arrows are dashed, and the best-evidenced thing the deck does is one of them.

So I will not tell you the flow is proven. I will tell you a checker-passed artifact walked that board and got 18 to 11, and you may do the arithmetic yourself.

The same gap sits on my side and it is larger.

Every figure I have quoted measures assembly. None measures lethality. Nothing says how many upkeeps this clock needs to kill one opponent, or how often the deck gets them. The route this deck wins with in most of the games it wins has no rate at all.

What does have a rate is the other one. The Aetherflux Reservoir kill assembles in 0.7% of games. 2.4% with the deck's one modelled tutor. 0.3% by turn six, mean turn 6.809. And 0.7% is a ceiling rather than a rate: the requirement is written as one rock, Sol Ring or Arcane Signet, and the loop needs both. Every game the simulation counted on one rock is a game the record says does not loop.

Four stacks fence that line off, and the fencing is the useful part.

Stack 001: Hullbreaker Horror and Sol Ring alone, no loop — the trigger locks its target while the artifact you cast is still a spell, so the pair does nothing repeatable. The famous two-card infinite printed against this deck is not one.

Stack 004: add the second rock. Each cast's trigger returns the OTHER rock, a permanent at that moment, and the cycle is exactly mana-neutral — three spent, three produced. Unbounded casts, and on its own no mana, no cards and no damage.

Stack 005: Displacer Kitten does not make it mana-positive.

Stack 006: the Reservoir on top. From 32 life, fifteen casts is the proven minimum — fourteen fails at minus thirteen — funding three activations at 50 life apiece, three opponents dead in one main phase, you left on 2. And 006 is honest about the price: every loop cast and every activation opens a fully open priority window, and Hullbreaker protects none of them — activating is not casting. Those opponents had empty boards and did nothing, and Grand Abolisher was in the 99 and not on the battlefield.

Then count what that turn asks for. A named single card is 7.1% of an opening seven. The kill wants two of them — Hullbreaker Horror and the Reservoir — plus a rock pair, plus the Abolisher the Counselor just named, in one main phase.

Hullbreaker Horror is the deck's only single point of failure: 7.1% of openers, 9.1% by turn three, and Long-Term Plans is the one card in the 99 that can search him out.

The mana to hold a window open is the reliable half. Free or cheap interaction is eight cards: 45.6% of openers, held in 78.1% of games, 67.2% by turn six, mean turn 2.764 — second only to the donation engine. The commander is cast by turn six in 90.2% of games, mean turn 4.133.

Which is exactly how to treat the kill: as something that happens TO you, not something you are waiting for.

You do not build a turn around it. You do not go hunting for it while three people are drawing cards you could have been charging for. The piece shows up, the table taps low, the Abolisher is already down — then you go, and not one beat earlier. Count their untapped mana first and assume every answer at that table appears the second you present lethal, because it does.

And hold the counter FOR the go turn, not after it. After it there is no game left to protect.

There is a third way out of this deck, by the way, and nobody plans for it because it looks exactly like losing.

You mean drawing from an empty library, and it is a route rather than a rider.

Jace, Wielder of Mysteries replaces the loss with a win: if you would draw with no library, you win instead. It is a replacement effect, not a trigger — no stack, no window for anybody, and worth nothing at all unless he is already on the battlefield at the moment the draw would happen. And the deck can genuinely get there: Font of Mythos gives every player two extra cards each draw step, three more permanents give one, the two doublers double every draw after your first, and Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics all read "target player" — you are a legal target for your own X-draw.

That is printed text and I label it as such. No stack in this deck has walked it. I can tell you the rule that would apply. I cannot tell you it has been checked.

And I cannot tell you when. The simulation runs ten turns of resource development and never counts a library, so there is no figure for the turn this deck empties itself — not a small one, none.

The win conditions do have one number, with a caveat the file attaches to it. Five cards, 31.2% of openers, 61.2% of games, 50.5% by turn six, 68.0% with the tutor, mean turn 3.083 — and that group mixes three finishers with two tutors, so it prices a finisher or something that finds one. A Mystical Tutor with nothing to point at is not access to a win.

Fine. Then sit down expecting to win on upkeeps and take everything else as a present.

Here is your game. Land something that charges before you open the tap wide. Give cards away on other people's turns, not in their draw steps. Hold two mana at their upkeep and make the Maiden count one more. Keep the counter for the turn you actually go. And let the table watch you do nothing for six turns while two artifacts nobody has thought about in years take them apart three and four points at a time.

When your own library gets thin, do not panic and do not apologise. Check whether the Jace is somewhere you can reach — in this deck, running out is one of the exits.
